supporting_evidence.quote: Automotive sales revenue decreased $6.66 billion, or 9%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, due a decrease of approximately 8% in cash deliveries and a lower average selling price per unit driven by sales mix and higher customer incentives such as attractive financing options.

The mathematical relationship doesn't contradict the claim that pricing was a primary driver - both volume and pricing were significant contributors.

The evidence shows regulatory credits affected gross margin but were not identified as a primary driver of the automotive sales revenue decline itself. The filing distinguishes between "automotive sales revenue" and "automotive regulatory credits revenue" as separate line items.

E1 explicitly states the decline was "due" to deliveries and lower average selling price, with sales mix being a component of the pricing effect.
